text:
anil: quick brain dump — i've been thinking about score normalization across tenants. current policy graph mixes raw cost and latency scores and larger tenants win because they dominate signal. want to propose a normalized scoring layer.
zoe: can you explain the problem with an example?
anil: sure. tenant A (huge QPS) has small latency preference but low budget. tenant B (small QPS) wants low-latency and is willing to pay. compiler currently aggregates global cost/latency histograms and picks weights; A's volume skews buckets so B often loses hedges.
marc: so the ask is to make weighting tenant-aware? risk is complexity & instability.
anil: exactly. proposal: compute per-tenant normalized z-scores for each metric (latency, cost, region_penalty) relative to tenant-specific baselines, then combine with tenant-priority multiplier to produce final route_score. this keeps tiny tenants' preferences visible.
rachel: z-scores might be noisy for low-volume tenants (std dev small). what's the smoothing plan?
anil: use hierarchical smoothing: for tenants with <N samples, shrink towards cohort mean using Bayesian shrinkage (alpha parameter). also add minimum sample floor and time-decay window.
zoe: how to keep scoring comparable across tenants for routing decisions? we need a canonical space.
anil: normalized scores map to a fixed range (-3..+3). compiler then applies a tenant_priority_scale (from SLA/contract) and a global tradeoff lambda to synthesize a global cost function: final_score = lambda_lat * norm_lat + lambda_cost * norm_cost * tenant_scale. decisions still passed to runtime for compat checks.
marc: interesting. what about fairness across regions and model variants? regional baselines differ a lot.
anil: (typo) oops. anil: we include region-aware baselines: compute norm per (tenant, region, model_family) cell where data exists; fall back to tenant-level then cohort-level. model-variant penalties become additive offsets to norm_cost so variants aren't underweighted.
rachel: rollout and telemetry? need to prove no regressions.
anil: simulation plan: replay 30d traffic and compute route changes, probe_count, cost_delta, p50/p95 latency per-tenant. shadow run in pre-prod for 7d where compiler emits both old_score and new_score and runtime collects which route would be chosen. metrics: per_tenant_winners_change_rate, swap_rate_for_high_sla_tenants, cost_shift_percentile, and discrepancy_rate where runtime-adj combined differs.
ops-bot: deploy-check: shadow must sample 100% traces for top 100 tenants and 5% for others.
zoe: safety thresholds?
anil: gate: high-sla tenants (p95 SLO) must not see >0.2% latency regression; false_positive_filter (where normalization causes valid routes to be removed) < 0.01%. also track stability: per-tenant route churn (target <1% daily).
marc: computation cost concerns — per-tenant, per-region stats across millions of tenants could be heavy. solution?
anil: maintain online aggregates with exponential decay. use sketching (t-digest for latencies, CMS for counts). compute z-score approx via mean/std maintained online. for ultra-low-volume tenants, use cohort proxies to avoid per-tenant state.
rachel: explainability? oncall will need to know why a route lost.
anil: add reason codes showing normalization contributions: e.g., norm_lat:-1.2, norm_cost:+0.8, tenant_scale:0.6, final_score:-0.13. wire into tracelets and full provenance blobs. include a /debug/score_breakdown endpoint.
zoe: config knobs?
anil: sample config for RFC:
```
policy.normalization.enabled = true
policy.normalization.cohort_size = 50
policy.normalization.shrinkage_alpha = 0.7
policy.normalization.decay_half_life = "6h"
policy.normalization.lambda_lat = 0.6
policy.normalization.lambda_cost = 0.4
policy.normalization.min_samples = 20
policy.normalization.white_list = ["tenant:enterprise-x"]
```
marc: migration path? can't flip globally.
anil: staged rollout: 1) compiler shadow mode only (emit both scores) for 7d; 2) enable for cohort tenants (non-critical) in pre-prod edges for 3d; 3) small canary in prod for 1% traffic; 4) monitor metrics and ramp. rollback via feature flag at compiler.
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-5201 created for metric dashboards and t-digest libs: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/INFRA-5201
rachel: one more failure mode: if cohort baselines get polluted by attack or bulk changes (e.g., new region spinup), normalization could mislead. add anomaly detection on cohort stats and automatic rollback to global baseline if detected.
anil: good call. we'll add `cohort_stability_check` and scoreboard alerts.
zoe: please include evaluation script and sample dashboards in the RFC. also add a nightly job to recompute cohort mappings to avoid stale cohorts.
anil: will do. i'll draft RFC with math, pseudocode, simulation results from offline run, and playbook. scheduling architecture sync next Friday. thanks all.
